children: Burlington, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - October 8, 2026) - Silver Bullet Mines Corp.

(OTCQB: SBMCF) ("SBMI" or "the Company") is pleased to announce significant assay results from various locations at the Columbia / Gold Queen Complex in Arizona. These results are guiding the Company towards production of higher-grade saleable concentrate from its mill in Globe, Arizona.
To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

The Columbia / Gold Queen Complex is comprised of the past producing Columbia Mine, the past producing Gold Queen Mine, the past producing Steamboat Mine (the existence of which the Company was previously unaware), at least four other newly-discovered potential high grade gold zones, and large stockpiles built by unknown parties likely from the Gold Queen.

Historically, all material taken from the Gold Queen had been carried out by mule. An average healthy pack mule was able to carry out 200 pounds of dead weight over a sustained journey, meaning the material then taken from the Gold Queen had to be sufficiently endowed to economically justify the trip.
Map of New Road Connecting to Existing Highway
To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

SBMI has built a road to the Columbia Mine and is completing a road to the Gold Queen Mine. This is the first road to the Gold Queen, meaning the Company is the first to bring modern mining equipment and methods to bear on the mine, including having a 25-ton truck able to haul material.
New Road Being Completed to Gold Queen Mine
To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:
The ongoing sampling and assay program is providing significant results from the Columbia, Gold Queen and Steamboat Mines, as well as from a stockpile proximate to the Gold Queen.

Assay results from various sites at the Complex are below. (For all of the samples referred to below, readers are cautioned samples are random by nature and may not be representative of their location or of the Complex generally.)
Assay Results from Steamboat Mine Samples

On re-discovering the Steamboat Mine, the field team collected crumbly channel chip samples from the roof near the portal from a pinch and swell 0.5 to 1 metre wide vein and from another 2 metre wide vein approximately 7-10 metres away. These samples were sent to Activation Laboratories, an independent accredited lab, for analysis. Results for the first eight samples have been received and returned anomalous gold values. The other 5 samples were anomalous for gold, silver and copper.

Assay Results from Concentrate from Steamboat Stockpile Material

In its news release of October 6, 2026 SBMI announced it had produced roughly six thousand pounds of concentrate from a stockpile near the new road. This material has shown to be very suitable to be processed at SBMI's mill. The Company is awaiting assay results from a third party lab from that concentrate.

The samples referred to above were taken over an area of roughly 400 acres (169.9 hectares). Field observations indicate the mineralization is widely spread throughout the Complex in numerous quartz veins and gossans.

The field team reports the Columbia adit follows a nearly vertical variably mineralized fault structure. Host rock is diabase to the back face. Quartzite contact overhead gently angles down toward the adit roof. Limestone appears to overlay the quartzite. The amount of veinlet quartz and associated bleb copper oxide appears to increase as the adit progresses to the back. Some form of sulfide as tiny blebs in the vein quartz is also in evidence.
The faulted vein structure boundary is marked by two to four inches of conspicuous orange-brown gossan locally cut by numerous hairline quartz veinlets.

The field team has observed vertical, close to east-west trending fault structures that assumingly guided the emplacement of multiple veins. It is possible there will be an intersection of the mineralized structure the adit is following with a series of east-west oriented veins, and at such an intersection one could expect to find 'chimneys' of mineralized material.
In addition to the above, rusty parallel quartz veins were observed in the construction of the newly constructed road bed. Panning revealed native gold and ruby silver.
In brief, the area has significant gold mineralization over an extensive area that warrants further evaluation.

Mr. Robert G. Komarechka, P.Geo., an independent consultant, has reviewed, verified and approved SBMI's work referred to herein and is the Qualified Person for this release as per TSXV requirements and
3.1. The QP was not at the site for sample collection which was undertaken by the SBMI field crew.

Samples were brought to the SBMI mill site where they were crushed prior to shipping. The crushed samples were then packaged and hand delivered to a courier in Globe, Arizona and shipped to Activation Laboratories in Ancaster Ontario, an ISO SCC accredited ISO/TEC 17025.2017 laboratory.
The following analytical packages were requested: QOP PGE-OES (Fire Assay ICPOES), QOP 1F2 (Total Digestion ICPOES), and QOP UT-8 (Sodium Peroxide Fusion ICPOE).
Certified standards and blanks were run by the laboratory.
QA/QC from SBMI Lab in Globe, Arizona

The samples from the stockpiles were analyzed by SBMI at its in-house facility near Globe, Arizona. These samples were processed through the Lab Jaw Crusher, Lab Hammer Mill and Splitter Box into an aliquot. Most of the pulverized aliquot was mixed with a flux and flour combination and melted in a crucible at 1,850 degree Fahrenheit, with the remainder being logged and archived. Upon cooling, the poured melt was in the form of a metal button and slag, following which a bone ash cupel was utilized to eliminate the lead in the button to form a bead. The bead was then weighed, following which a solution of 6 to 1 distilled water to nitric acid was utilized to dissolve the gold in the bead at approximately 175 degrees Fahrenheit.
